options.text: Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Isotopes have the same number of electrons but different numbers of protons.
Isotopes differ in the number of protons while having the same number of neutrons.
Isotopes are atoms that have gained or lost electrons, giving them a charge.

items.explanation: Isotopes share the same proton count (same element) and differ only in neutron number; the other choices mix up electrons or proton differences.

items.stem: Element Y has atomic number 15. Two atoms of Y have mass numbers 31 and 33. Which description is correct?

options.text: Both atoms are isotopes of element Y.
The atom with mass number 31 is an isotope, and the one with 33 is an ion.
Mass number does not affect isotopic identity, so neither is an isotope.
Only the atom with mass number 33 is an isotope because it has more neutrons.

items.explanation: Atoms with the same proton number but different mass numbers are isotopes; ions involve a gain or loss of electrons, not a change in mass number.

items.stem: A museum displays a sample labeled $^{235}\text{U}$ and a sodium sample labeled $Na^{+}$. Which pairing correctly identifies each as an isotope or an ion?

options.text: $^{235}\text{U}$ is an isotope of uranium; $Na^{+}$ is a sodium ion.
$^{235}\text{U}$ is a sodium ion; $Na^{+}$ is an isotope of sodium.
$^{235}\text{U}$ is an ion because it has a charge; $Na^{+}$ is an isotope because its mass number differs from $Na$.
$^{235}\text{U}$ is an isotope; $Na^{+}$ is a neutral atom.

items.explanation: $^{235}\text{U}$ differs from other uranium atoms only in neutron count (an isotope), while $Na^{+}$ has lost an electron, giving it a positive charge (an ion).
